I was born in the small Georgian town of Gori, nestled at the foot of the Caucasus mountains. It was a humble place — dusty streets, stone houses, and the great fortress looming above everything else. My earliest memories are of Gori’s winding lanes and the little home I shared with my mother. The place shaped me in ways I could not have understood as a child.

I was born in the year 1878, in the small Georgian town of Gori. My mother, Keke, raised me alone—my father was absent. The memories of my earliest years are filled with both hardship and warmth, colored by her love amidst poverty. My upbringing in Gori, those first tentative steps in a church school, and the later move to a seminary shaped much of my character and beliefs. The pain of leaving her haunted me for years—and in many ways, has never left me.
